cases.purpose: lsblk lists a loop device with a device-mapper child (dm linear over loop) with TYPE loop/dm, matching sizes and parent-child tree in tree, list, no-deps, raw and pairs forms, like util-linux.
cases.oracle: util-linux lsblk reading the same loop and device-mapper nodes (device names normalised); sizes, FSTYPE and mountpoints come from the kernel and the on-device superblock.
cases.comparison: Byte parity of status, stdout, stderr and file tree.
cases.script:
. ./rl.sh
r() { local l=$1; shift; "$@" >o.txt 2>e.txt; local rc=$?; printf '[%s] status=%s\n' "$l" $rc; norm o.txt; echo "[stderr]"; norm e.txt; }
/usr/bin/truncate -s 4M b.img; at b.img; B=$REPLY; $MK -q -t ext2 -L LSFS $B
reg $B LOOP-B
sectors=$(/usr/sbin/blockdev --getsz $B)
printf '0 %s linear %s 0\n' $sectors $B | /usr/sbin/dmsetup create --noudevsync w7dm
r loop-tree lsblk -o NAME,TYPE,SIZE,RO $B
r loop-list lsblk -l -o NAME,TYPE,SIZE $B
r loop-nodeps lsblk -d -o NAME,TYPE,SIZE,RO $B
r loop-raw lsblk -r -n -o NAME,TYPE $B
r dm-only lsblk -o NAME,TYPE,SIZE /dev/mapper/w7dm
r pairs lsblk -P -o NAME,TYPE $B

cases.purpose: FSTYPE, LABEL and MOUNTPOINT columns of a loop device holding ext2 are read from the superblock and /proc/self/mounts, before mounting, while mounted and after umount, like util-linux.
cases.oracle: util-linux lsblk reading the same loop and device-mapper nodes (device names normalised); sizes, FSTYPE and mountpoints come from the kernel and the on-device superblock.
cases.comparison: Byte parity of status, stdout, stderr and file tree.
cases.script:
. ./rl.sh
r() { local l=$1; shift; "$@" >o.txt 2>e.txt; local rc=$?; printf '[%s] status=%s\n' "$l" $rc; norm o.txt; echo "[stderr]"; norm e.txt; }
/usr/bin/truncate -s 4M b.img; at b.img; B=$REPLY; $MK -q -t ext2 -L LSMNT $B
reg $B LOOP-B
/usr/bin/mkdir -p mnt
r unmounted lsblk -o NAME,FSTYPE,LABEL,MOUNTPOINT $B
/usr/bin/mount $B mnt
r mounted lsblk -o NAME,FSTYPE,LABEL,MOUNTPOINT $B
r mounted-fs lsblk -f $B
r mounted-raw lsblk -r -n -o NAME,FSTYPE,MOUNTPOINT $B
/usr/bin/umount mnt
r after-umount lsblk -o NAME,FSTYPE,MOUNTPOINT $B
